comments.body:
## MEASURED-738A-A: it is the CODE, not an agent forcing — and my "no non-force remedy" was imprecise

Investigated against the close code and the whole store rather than the two tickets in front of me.
Three corrections, one of them to this ticket's own framing.

### 1. 0059 was NOT forced. 2bc7 WAS. The earlier reopen conflated them.

The discriminator is **not** the STATUS event's shape — I initially read it that way and it is wrong.
`force_close` is recorded as an audit COMMENT (`transition_close.py:754`), never as a status-event
field, so both a forced and an unforced close leave the identical event keys
`['close_class','current_status','parent_status_uuid','status']`. 2bc7's original close event looks
exactly like 0059's, and 2bc7 *was* forced.

Counting the actual audit record across each ticket's full history, retired events included:

```
0059  FORCE_CLOSE records: 0     close_class = duplicate     <- a sanctioned disposition
2bc7  FORCE_CLOSE records: 1     close_class = preexisting   <- an agent bypassing the gate
```

`preexisting` is **not** in `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES`, so 2bc7 genuinely owed completion
verification, could not satisfy the referencing-commit precheck (its fix landed under J4's commit,
which names ticket 0a94, not 2bc7), and was forced past it. That one is agent behaviour.

0059 took the exemption at `transition_close.py:253-260` as designed and never owed a completion
verdict at all. **So the reopen rationale — "closed WITHOUT a completion-verifier attestation … so it
never passed the gate", applied to both tickets — was correct for 2bc7 and false for 0059.** 0059
never needed to pass that gate. Reopening it rested on a premise that did not hold for it.

### 2. A duplicate CAN be certified — but only if it hides its replacement

Measured over every disposition-closed bug in the store (21 of them):

```
close_class in {duplicate, not_a_bug, escalated}
  WITH a live `duplicates` link   ->  7 of 7 UNSIGNED
                                      0059, 6ba6, 82c4, cabc, df2c, e47e, e519
  WITHOUT one                     ->  7 CERTIFIED
                                      0cfd, 2322, 2ea4, 368a, 3a17, 480e, 7f6c, cf19
```

The link is exactly what trips `_has_live_replacement_link` and skips the verifier. So the
attestation is reachable **precisely for the worse-documented duplicates** — record which ticket
supersedes you and you forfeit certification; stay silent about it and you get signed. That
inversion is the defect, and it is sharper than the version this ticket was filed with.

### 3. Correcting this ticket: "no non-force remedy" was imprecise

There IS a non-force path — delete the `duplicates` link — and I listed it among the dishonest
escapes without noticing it is the *same* lever the exemption keys on. The accurate statement is
narrower and worse: **the only way to certify an honestly-linked duplicate is to stop declaring it a
duplicate.**

### 4. Why this stayed invisible: the docstring does not mention the branch

`_completion_precheck`'s docstring says it returns the sign signal "or ``None`` when the gate is off
or the close is a ``--force-close``". The disposition branch added a THIRD `None` path and the
docstring was never updated, so the function's contract still reads as "unsigned implies off or
forced" — which is exactly the inference the reopen made, and exactly the inference
`child_closure_findings` encodes when it treats any unsigned closure as uncertified.

### Bearing on epic e369

The epic's certification is withheld by two descendants, and they are different in kind:

* **0059** — correctly closed, unsigned by design. Blocked by THIS defect. Not remediable by any
  honest agent action.
* **b586** — `stale-material`: its completion signature is `certified` but `compute_validity` rejects
  it because the ticket was materially edited after the verdict. Remediable by re-closing.

So an operator ruling here is load-bearing for closing e369, and the ruling is narrower than I first
wrote: it is about whether a declared replacement link should FORWARD certification rather than
forfeit it.

comments.body:
## FIXED-738A-B: implemented per the operator's ruling — Gerrit 1378, verified end-to-end

Ruling: *update the close gate to provide attestation for duplicates with a live link.* Done.

### Shape of the fix

A disposition close now returns a **sign signal** instead of `None`, so the existing signing path
mints the op-cert with no special-casing at the call site. It is **deterministic — no LLM call**,
because there is still nothing to verify; the exemption's original justification is untouched.

**The manifest does not claim a completion PASS.** That was the design constraint I would not trade
away: a signature reading `completion-verifier: PASS` for a ticket whose completion was never
verified is a lie in the signed bytes, and an auditor could no longer distinguish a verified
completion from a bookkeeping disposition. What 0059 now actually carries:

```
completion-verifier: DISPOSITION duplicate
replacement: 23ed-de0a-765b-49aa
ticket: 0059-c7f0-cce1-4077
model: none (deterministic disposition)
runner: close_disposition
rebar-version: 0.10.1
material: 48469f827ce62b75
```

`kind` is derived as the text before the first `": "` (`reducer/_processors_identity.py`), so this is
still a `completion-verifier` record and `verify_signature(kind="completion-verifier")` finds it. The
`material:` step is preserved, so validity-on-read still invalidates it after a post-verdict edit —
identical semantics to a verified completion, not a permanently-valid special case.

### Verified END TO END, not just in units

```
verify_signature(0059, kind="completion-verifier")  ->  certified
child_closure_findings(e369)  ->  uncertified 2 -> 1   (only b586 remains)
```

### All three exempt classes, because two were LATENT

Measured before the fix: only `duplicate` had closes carrying a live link (7 of them, all unsigned).
`not_a_bug` had **zero** linked closes and `escalated` had **zero closed bugs at all** — so both sat
on the identical code path and would have produced the identical gap the first time one was linked.
The fix keys on the same class-set + link predicate, so they are covered before that happens rather
than after. The remaining no-code-change classes (`flaky`, `env_integration`, `undetermined`,
`preexisting`) are NOT dispositions: they still run the verifier and were already being certified, so
widening the set to them would have removed real verification.

### `--force-close` still withholds the signature, and that is now pinned

Its guard runs BEFORE the disposition branch, so a `--force-close --class duplicate` on a linked bug
produces no sign signal. That ordering is load-bearing now in a way it was not before — if reversed,
the operator's escape hatch would become a way to certify without verifying. **Mutation-checked:**
moving the guard after the disposition branch makes the new test fail with exactly that message;
restoring it makes it pass. A guarantee asserted without a demonstrated RED would have been worth
little here.

### Placement

The logic is a new module (`_commands/close_disposition.py`) rather than more lines in
`transition_close.py`, which is at its size ceiling and is being split by another session; the call
site there changes by two lines and `_verdict_manifest` gains a three-line delegation.

# A bug closed as a DUPLICATE withholds its parent's certification forever, with no non-force remedy

## The two halves of the gate disagree

**The close path grants dispositions an exemption.** `_commands/transition_close.py:253-260`:

> A duplicate / not-a-bug / escalated bug with a durable replacement relation is a disposition, not
> a claim that this ticket's acceptance criteria were implemented. Skip the completion-only checks
> (including file-impact and the billable verifier) [...]

So `rebar transition <bug> in_progress closed --class duplicate` returns exit 0 and mints **no**
`completion-verifier` attestation. That is correct and deliberate: a duplicate never claimed to
implement its own ACs, so verifying its completion would be meaningless (and billable).

**The certification path does not honor that exemption.** `llm/completion.py:170-199`
(`child_closure_findings`) requires a valid `completion-verifier` attestation on **every** closed
direct child, with no disposition branch. A disposition-closed child therefore lands in
`uncertified`, and `gate_ops.py:131`'s `certifiable = not uncertified` withholds the parent's
signature.

## Why this is a trap, not merely an inconvenience

The two rules are each individually right and compose into a state with **no non-force exit**:

* the child cannot earn an attestation — reopening and re-closing takes the same exemption branch
  every time, so the outcome is identical on every attempt;
* `--force-close` produces exactly the uncertified state the operator ruling prohibits;
* the only other escapes are dishonest: pick a close class that is not the true disposition, delete
  the true `duplicates` link, or de-parent the child so it leaves `children`. Each makes the tree
  certify by misrepresenting it.

## Live instance, with the substance intact

Epic `e369-a449-4773-48fb` (Jira DC support). Child `0059-c7f0-cce1-4077` is a true duplicate of
`23ed-de0a-765b-49aa` — the same defect diagnosed to its actual cause, fixed and merged as change
1124. Measured just now:

```
child_closure_findings('e369-a449-4773-48fb')
  UNCERTIFIED: child 0059 is closed but its completion closure is not certified/valid
               (signature: unsigned)
verify_signature('23ed-de0a-765b-49aa', kind='completion-verifier') -> certified
```

**The replacement is certified AND is a direct sibling under the same epic.** So the work IS attested
inside this tree; the gate simply will not look through the `duplicates` edge to find it. The epic is
denied certification over a bookkeeping gap, not a missing verification.

## Candidate remedy — NOT to be applied without an operator ruling

Teach `child_closure_findings` the same disposition branch the close path already has: when a closed
child carries a disposition class (`duplicate` / `not_a_bug` / `escalated`) **and** a net-active
replacement link to a live ticket, resolve certification **through** that link — certified iff the
replacement's own closure is certified-and-valid — rather than demanding an attestation the child is
exempt from producing. `_has_live_replacement_link` already implements the predicate, so both halves
could share one definition instead of drifting.

**Why this is an operator ruling and not an agent's call:** it changes when a parent close is
certifiable, which is gate semantics — the same class of decision as the degrade-open remedy on
[rebar:1019-e1e9-5117-4795] and [rebar:2a76]. A wrong call here either keeps blocking honest closes
or lets an unattested subtree certify by pointing at an unrelated ticket. Recording it rather than
fixing it unilaterally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] the operator rules on whether disposition-closed children resolve certification through their
      replacement link, or must remain uncertified by design — **RULED: attest them.**
- [x] `child_closure_findings` and the close gate share ONE definition of "disposition with a live
      replacement": `close_disposition.DISPOSITION_CLASSES` is asserted equal to
      `close_precheck._NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` — verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py`
- [x] a disposition close MINTS a `completion-verifier` attestation, and its manifest does NOT claim a
      completion PASS that never happened (it reads `DISPOSITION <class>` + the replacement id)
- [x] the negative case still holds: NO live replacement link ⇒ no attestation, so the close keeps
      normal verification and `--class duplicate` cannot become a bypass
- [x] `--force-close` remains UNSIGNED — its guard runs before the disposition branch, mutation-checked
      by reverting the guard's position and observing the test fail
- [x] the wiring is exercised through the REAL `_completion_precheck`, not only the module in isolation
      (the call site moved during bug 74a3's split; a piece-only suite stayed green through the move)
- [x] end-to-end: `verify_signature(0059, kind="completion-verifier")` returns `certified` and epic
      e369's uncertified descendant count drops from 2 to 1

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py -q      # 17 passed
    pytest tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py tests/unit/test_compute_validity.py \
           tests/unit/test_transition_close.py -q                        # 59 passed
    make lint && make typecheck                                          # clean

Mutation checks performed (a guard asserted without a demonstrated RED is unverified):

* force-close ordering — moved `if force_close: return None` AFTER the disposition branch;
  `test_a_force_close_is_still_never_signed_even_for_a_linked_duplicate` FAILS. Restored: passes.
* call-site wiring — reverted the disposition branch to `return None`;
  `test_the_precheck_ACTUALLY_returns_the_disposition_verdict` FAILS. Restored: passes.

End-to-end verification was run against the real store (reopen → claim → close `--class duplicate`),
producing the manifest recorded in the FIXED-738A-B comment.

file_impact.reason: deterministic disposition attestation: replacement lookup, verdict shaped as the sign signal, manifest decoration that does not claim a completion PASS
disposition branch returns the sign signal instead of None; _verdict_manifest delegates decoration
all three exempt classes, fail-closed without a link, manifest honesty, and the mutation-checked force-close ordering guarantee
